flyers-necklace.definition: a piece of jewellery worn around the neck
flyers-necklace.hint: A necklace can be made of beads, gold, or shells.
flyers-necklace.fact: People have worn necklaces for thousands of years.

flyers-nest.definition: a place birds build to lay their eggs
flyers-nest.hint: Birds build a nest from twigs and leaves.
flyers-nest.fact: Some birds build a new nest every single year.

flyers-news.definition: information about things that have just happened
flyers-news.hint: Grown-ups often watch the news in the evening.
flyers-news.fact: News can come from TV, newspapers, radio, or the internet.

flyers-newspaper.definition: printed sheets of paper with news stories
flyers-newspaper.hint: A newspaper is printed with new stories every day.
flyers-newspaper.fact: Newspapers have been telling people the news for hundreds of years.

flyers-next.hint: What is the next lesson after break time?

flyers-noisy.definition: making a lot of loud sound

flyers-north.definition: the direction to your left when facing the sunrise

flyers-nowhere.definition: not in, at, or to any place

flyers-ocean.definition: a huge area of salty sea water
flyers-ocean.hint: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean on Earth.
flyers-ocean.fact: Oceans cover more than two-thirds of our planet.

flyers-octopus.definition: a sea animal with eight long arms
flyers-octopus.hint: An octopus can change colour to hide from danger.

flyers-of-course.definition: used to say yes in a strong, friendly way
flyers-of-course.hint: Say 'of course!' when the answer is clearly yes.
flyers-of-course.fact: 'Of course' shows you are very happy to agree.

flyers-office.definition: a room or building where people do desk work
flyers-office.hint: Many grown-ups work at a desk in an office.
flyers-office.fact: An office often has desks, computers, and telephones.

flyers-olives.definition: small green or black fruits used in cooking
flyers-olives.hint: Olives grow on trees in warm countries.
flyers-olives.fact: Oil made from olives is called olive oil.

flyers-once.definition: one time, or at some time in the past
flyers-once.hint: Say 'once upon a time' to start a fairy tale.
flyers-once.fact: 'Once' can mean 'one time' or 'in the past'.

flyers-online.hint: You can read books or play games online.
flyers-online.fact: Being online means your device is connected to the internet.

flyers-oven.definition: an enclosed space used to bake or roast food
flyers-oven.hint: We bake a cake in a hot oven.
flyers-oven.fact: Ovens can be part of a cooker or a separate machine.

flyers-over.hint: Say 'the film is over' when it has finished.
flyers-over.fact: 'Over' can mean above, across, or finished.

flyers-p-m-pajamas.definition: soft, comfortable clothes worn for sleeping
flyers-p-m-pajamas.hint: You put on pajamas before you go to bed.

flyers-passenger.definition: a person travelling in a car, bus, plane, or train
flyers-passenger.hint: A passenger does not drive the vehicle.
flyers-passenger.fact: Big planes can carry hundreds of passengers at once.

flyers-past.hint: History lessons teach us about the past.

flyers-path.definition: a narrow track for people to walk along
flyers-path.hint: Follow the path through the park to the lake.
flyers-path.fact: Paths in a forest are often made just by people walking.

flyers-pepper.definition: a spice or vegetable used to add flavour to food
flyers-pepper.hint: A little pepper adds a strong flavour to soup.
flyers-pepper.fact: Black pepper comes from small dried berries.

flyers-perhaps.hint: Say 'perhaps' when you are not completely sure.
flyers-perhaps.fact: 'Perhaps' and 'maybe' mean almost the same thing.

flyers-photographer.definition: a person whose job is taking photographs
flyers-photographer.hint: A photographer uses a camera to capture special moments.
flyers-photographer.fact: Photographers can work at weddings, in nature, or for magazines.

flyers-piece.hint: Ask for a piece of cake, please.
flyers-piece.fact: A puzzle is made of many small pieces.

flyers-pilot.definition: a person who flies a plane
flyers-pilot.hint: A pilot sits at the front of the plane to fly it.
flyers-pilot.fact: Pilots train for years before they can fly a passenger plane.

flyers-pizza.definition: a flat, round bread with cheese and toppings, baked
flyers-pizza.hint: You can put many toppings, like cheese, on a pizza.
flyers-pizza.fact: Pizza first became popular in Naples, Italy.

flyers-planet.definition: a huge round object in space that circles a star
flyers-planet.hint: Earth is the planet we live on.
flyers-planet.fact: There are eight planets in our solar system.

flyers-plastic.definition: made of a light, man-made material
flyers-plastic.hint: A plastic cup is light and does not break easily.
flyers-plastic.fact: Plastic can take hundreds of years to break down.

flyers-platform.definition: the raised area where you wait for a train
flyers-platform.hint: Wait behind the yellow line on the platform.
flyers-platform.fact: Big train stations can have many different platforms.

flyers-pleased.definition: feeling happy and satisfied about something
flyers-pleased.hint: Say 'pleased to meet you' when you meet someone new.
flyers-pleased.fact: 'Pleased' is a polite way of saying you are happy.

flyers-pocket.definition: a small bag sewn into clothes to hold things
flyers-pocket.hint: You can keep small things, like keys, in your pocket.
flyers-pocket.fact: Some clothes have several pockets for different things.

flyers-police-officer.definition: a person whose job is to keep people safe from crime
flyers-police-officer.hint: A police officer wears a special uniform.
flyers-police-officer.fact: Police officers help people who are lost or in danger too.

flyers-police-station.definition: a building where police officers work
flyers-police-station.hint: You can report a problem at the police station.
flyers-police-station.fact: Police officers start and end their working day at the station.

flyers-pond.definition: a small area of still water, smaller than a lake
flyers-pond.hint: Ducks often swim on a pond in the park.
flyers-pond.fact: A pond is much smaller than a lake or the sea.

flyers-poor.definition: having very little money, or deserving sympathy
flyers-poor.hint: Say 'poor dog' when an animal looks sad or hurt.

flyers-pop-music.definition: popular modern music with a catchy tune
flyers-pop-music.hint: Pop music is often played on the radio.

flyers-popular.definition: liked by a lot of people
flyers-popular.hint: Football is a very popular sport around the world.
flyers-popular.fact: A popular song is one that many people enjoy listening to.

flyers-post.definition: to send a letter or parcel by mail
flyers-post.hint: Put a stamp on the letter before you post it.
flyers-post.fact: You can also 'post' a message online to share with others.

flyers-post-office.definition: a place where you send letters and parcels
flyers-post-office.hint: Buy stamps at the post office before you post a letter.
flyers-post-office.fact: The post office also sells boxes for sending parcels.

flyers-postcard.definition: a card with a picture, sent by post without an envelope
flyers-postcard.hint: People send a postcard to friends while on holiday.
flyers-postcard.fact: Postcards usually have a photo of a place on the front.

flyers-prefer.definition: to like one thing more than another
flyers-prefer.hint: Say 'I prefer apples to bananas' to show what you like more.
flyers-prefer.fact: Everyone has different things they prefer to eat or do.

flyers-prepare.hint: Prepare your bag the night before school.
flyers-prepare.fact: Chefs prepare food carefully before they cook it.

flyers-prize.definition: something you win for doing well in a contest
flyers-prize.hint: The winner of the race gets a prize.
flyers-prize.fact: A prize can be a medal, a trophy, or even money.

flyers-problem.definition: something difficult that needs to be solved
flyers-problem.hint: Tell a grown-up if you have a problem you cannot solve.
flyers-problem.fact: Maths problems become easier the more you practise.

flyers-programme.definition: a show on TV or radio
flyers-programme.hint: What is your favourite TV programme?
flyers-programme.fact: 'Programme' can also mean a plan for an event.

flyers-project.definition: a piece of work you plan and research over time
flyers-project.hint: You might make a poster for a school project.
flyers-project.fact: Projects often let you choose a topic you find interesting.

flyers-pull.hint: Pull the door open instead of pushing it.

flyers-push.definition: to move something away from you using force
flyers-push.hint: Push the swing to make it go higher.

flyers-puzzle.definition: a game or toy that makes you think to solve it

flyers-puzzle.fact: A jigsaw puzzle can have hundreds of small pieces.

flyers-pyjamas.definition: soft, comfortable clothes worn for sleeping
flyers-pyjamas.hint: You put on pyjamas before you get into bed.
flyers-pyjamas.fact: Pyjamas usually have a top and matching trousers.

flyers-pyramid.definition: a large stone shape with a square base and pointed top
flyers-pyramid.hint: The pyramids in Egypt are thousands of years old.
flyers-pyramid.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built for an ancient king.

flyers-quarter.definition: one of four equal parts of something
flyers-quarter.hint: Cut the pizza into a quarter for each friend.
flyers-quarter.fact: 'Quarter past' means fifteen minutes after the hour.

flyers-queen.definition: a woman who rules a country, or a king's wife
flyers-queen.hint: A queen often wears a crown like a king does.
flyers-queen.fact: Some countries still have a queen who is part of the royal family.

flyers-quite.hint: Say 'quite tired' to mean fairly tired, not very tired.
flyers-quite.fact: 'Quite' can make a word a little stronger or weaker.

flyers-quiz.definition: a short test or game with questions
flyers-quiz.definitionVi: bài kiểm tra ngắn, trò chơi đố vui
flyers-quiz.hint: You answer questions quickly in a quiz.
flyers-quiz.fact: Quizzes are a fun way to check what you have learned.

flyers-race.definition: a competition to see who is fastest
flyers-race.hint: Runners line up at the start of a race.
flyers-race.fact: In a race, the winner crosses the finish line first.

flyers-bike.definition: connected with fast competitions, like a racing car
flyers-bike.definitionVi: thuộc về đua xe, tốc độ
flyers-bike.hint: A racing car is built to go extremely fast.
flyers-bike.fact: Racing bikes are made very light so riders can go faster.

flyers-railway.definition: the metal tracks that trains travel along
flyers-railway.hint: Trains travel along a railway to different towns.
flyers-railway.fact: The first railways were built about 200 years ago.

flyers-ready.definition: prepared and able to do something
flyers-ready.hint: Say 'I'm ready!' when you have everything you need.
flyers-ready.fact: Being ready early means you never have to rush.

flyers-remember.definition: to keep something in your mind and not forget it
flyers-remember.hint: Try to remember your homework every day.

flyers-repair.definition: to fix something that is broken
flyers-repair.hint: A mechanic can repair a broken bicycle.

flyers-repeat.definition: to say or do something again
flyers-repeat.hint: Ask 'Can you repeat that, please?' if you did not hear.
flyers-repeat.fact: Repeating new words helps you remember them better.

flyers-restaurant.definition: a place where people pay to eat a meal
flyers-restaurant.hint: You order food from a menu at a restaurant.
flyers-restaurant.fact: Restaurants can serve food from countries all around the world.

flyers-rich.fact: Being rich in friends and family is important too!

flyers-ring.definition: a piece of jewellery worn on a finger
flyers-ring.hint: A ring can be made of gold, silver, or plastic.
flyers-ring.fact: People often wear a special ring when they get married.

flyers-rock-music.definition: loud music with electric guitars and strong drums
flyers-rock-music.hint: Rock music often has a strong, fast beat.
flyers-rock-music.fact: Rock music became very popular around the 1950s and 1960s.

flyers-rocket.definition: a vehicle that flies fast into space
flyers-rocket.hint: A rocket blasts off with fire and smoke.
flyers-rocket.fact: Rockets have to travel very fast to escape Earth's gravity.

flyers-rucksack.definition: a bag carried on your back
flyers-rucksack.hint: You carry a rucksack when you go hiking or to school.
flyers-rucksack.fact: 'Rucksack' and 'backpack' mean almost the same thing.

flyers-salt.definition: a white food used to add flavour
flyers-salt.hint: A little salt makes food taste better.
flyers-salt.fact: The sea contains a huge amount of natural salt.

flyers-same.hint: Twins can wear the same clothes.

flyers-save.definition: to keep something safe, or to keep money
flyers-save.hint: Save your coins in a piggy bank.
flyers-save.fact: 'Save' can mean to keep money or to rescue someone.

flyers-science.definition: the school subject about how the world works
flyers-science.hint: In science, you might do experiments with water or plants.
flyers-science.fact: Science helps us understand animals, space, and the human body.

flyers-scissors.definition: a tool with two blades for cutting paper
flyers-scissors.hint: Use scissors carefully to cut along the line.
flyers-scissors.fact: Scissors have two blades joined together in the middle.

flyers-screen.definition: the flat surface of a TV, phone, or computer that shows pictures
flyers-screen.hint: You watch videos on a phone or TV screen.
flyers-screen.fact: Screens can show words, pictures, games, and videos.

flyers-search.definition: the act of trying to find something
flyers-search.hint: Do an online search to find the answer to a question.
flyers-search.fact: You can search the internet using just a few words.

flyers-secret.definition: something known only to a few people, kept hidden
flyers-secret.hint: Whisper a secret so only your friend can hear.
flyers-secret.fact: Everyone loves a good secret, especially about a surprise party!

flyers-sell.definition: to give something to someone who pays for it

flyers-several.definition: more than two, but not a huge number
flyers-several.hint: Say 'several times' to mean more than two or three times.
flyers-several.fact: 'Several' is more than 'a few' but less than 'many'.

flyers-shampoo.definition: a soapy liquid used to wash your hair
flyers-shampoo.hint: You use shampoo when you wash your hair in the shower.
flyers-shampoo.fact: Shampoo makes lots of bubbles when you rub it into wet hair.

flyers-shelf.definition: a flat board used to store or display things
flyers-shelf.hint: Put your books back on the shelf when you finish.
flyers-shelf.fact: A bookcase is made of several shelves joined together.

flyers-should.definition: used to give or ask for advice
flyers-should.hint: Say 'you should wear a coat' when it's cold outside.
flyers-should.fact: 'Should' is a gentle way to give someone advice.

flyers-silver.definition: having the colour of the shiny grey metal silver
flyers-silver.hint: The second-place winner often gets a silver medal.
flyers-silver.fact: Silver is a shiny metal often used to make jewellery.

flyers-singer.definition: a person whose job is to sing
flyers-singer.hint: A singer often performs songs on a stage.
flyers-singer.fact: Some singers write their own songs, too.

flyers-ski.definition: a long, flat board used to slide over snow
flyers-ski.hint: You wear a ski on each foot to glide over the snow.
flyers-ski.fact: People have used skis to travel over snow for thousands of years.

flyers-sledge.definition: a vehicle used to slide over snow, often for fun
flyers-sledge.hint: Children love to ride a sledge down a snowy hill.
flyers-sledge.fact: A sledge has no wheels — it slides on the snow.

flyers-smell.definition: something you notice with your nose
flyers-smell.hint: Fresh bread has a lovely smell.
flyers-smell.fact: Dogs can smell things far better than humans can.

flyers-snack.definition: a small amount of food eaten between meals
flyers-snack.hint: Fruit makes a healthy snack between meals.
flyers-snack.fact: A snack is smaller than a full meal.

flyers-snowball.definition: a ball made by pressing snow together
flyers-snowball.hint: Roll the snow in your hands to make a snowball.
flyers-snowball.fact: Snowballs are perfect for a friendly snowball fight.

flyers-snowboard.definition: a board used to slide down snowy hills standing up
flyers-snowboard.hint: You stand sideways on a snowboard as you slide down.
flyers-snowboard.fact: Snowboarding became an Olympic sport in 1998.

flyers-snowboarding.definition: the sport of sliding down snow on a snowboard
flyers-snowboarding.hint: You need a snowy mountain to go snowboarding.
flyers-snowboarding.fact: Snowboarding is a fun winter sport enjoyed all over the world.

flyers-snowman.definition: a figure of a person made from packed snow
flyers-snowman.hint: You can build a snowman with a carrot for a nose.
flyers-snowman.fact: A snowman melts away once the weather gets warmer.

flyers-so.definition: to a great degree, or as a result
flyers-so.hint: Say 'so happy' to mean very happy.
flyers-so.fact: 'So' can join two ideas or make a word stronger.

flyers-soap.definition: a substance used with water to clean your skin
flyers-soap.hint: Wash your hands with soap and water before you eat.
flyers-soap.fact: Soap makes bubbles that help wash dirt and germs away.

flyers-soft.definition: gentle to touch, not hard or rough
flyers-soft.hint: A pillow feels soft when you rest your head on it.

flyers-somewhere.definition: in, at, or to a place, not stated exactly

flyers-soon.hint: Say 'see you soon' when you will meet again shortly.
flyers-soon.fact: 'Soon' means something will happen before too long.

flyers-sore.hint: A sore throat can make it hurt to swallow.
flyers-sore.fact: Resting a sore muscle helps it feel better.

flyers-sound.hint: Music, voices, and thunder are all kinds of sound.
flyers-sound.fact: Sound travels through the air as invisible waves.

flyers-south.hint: Birds fly south to find warmer weather in winter.
flyers-south.fact: The South Pole is at the very bottom of the Earth.

flyers-space.definition: the huge area beyond Earth's sky with stars and planets
flyers-space.hint: Astronauts travel to space in a rocket.
flyers-space.fact: There is no air to breathe in space.

flyers-spaceship.definition: a vehicle that travels through space
flyers-spaceship.hint: A spaceship carries astronauts to the Moon or beyond.
flyers-spaceship.fact: Some spaceships have carried astronauts all the way to the Moon.

flyers-speak.hint: Speak clearly so everyone can understand you.
flyers-speak.fact: You can speak more than one language if you practise.

flyers-special.definition: different and better than usual, important
flyers-special.hint: Your birthday is a special day just for you.
flyers-special.fact: Special days, like festivals, are often full of celebration.

flyers-spend.definition: to use money to buy something, or to use time doing something
flyers-spend.hint: Don't spend all your pocket money at once.
flyers-spend.fact: You can spend money or spend time — both use the same word.

flyers-spoon.definition: a tool with a small bowl shape, used for eating
flyers-spoon.hint: You eat soup with a spoon.
flyers-spoon.fact: A spoon, fork, and knife are the main tools used at meals.

flyers-spot.hint: A ladybird has black spots on its red back.
flyers-spot.fact: Leopards and giraffes both have spots on their fur.

flyers-spotted.hint: A spotted dog has small marks all over its fur.
flyers-spotted.fact: Dalmatian dogs are famous for being spotted.

flyers-spring.definition: the season between winter and summer when flowers grow
flyers-spring.hint: Flowers and baby animals appear in spring.
flyers-spring.fact: Spring is when many plants start to grow again after winter.

flyers-stadium.definition: a large building with seats for watching sports
flyers-stadium.hint: Thousands of fans watch a match at a stadium.
flyers-stadium.fact: Some stadiums can hold more than one hundred thousand people.

flyers-stage-theatre.definition: the raised area where actors perform
flyers-stage-theatre.hint: Actors stand on the stage so the audience can see them.
flyers-stage-theatre.fact: Bright lights help everyone see the actors on the stage.

flyers-stamp.definition: a small sticker you put on post to pay for sending it
flyers-stamp.hint: Stick a stamp on the envelope before you post a letter.
flyers-stamp.fact: Some people collect stamps from different countries as a hobby.

flyers-stay.definition: to remain in a place and not leave
flyers-stay.hint: We will stay at a hotel during our holiday.
flyers-stay.fact: 'Stay' means you don't go anywhere else.

flyers-step.definition: a movement of the foot when walking, or a stair
flyers-step.hint: Take a big step to jump over the puddle.
flyers-step.fact: Walking up stairs means climbing one step at a time.

flyers-still.definition: continuing to happen, up until now
flyers-still.hint: Say 'I'm still hungry' if you want more food.
flyers-still.fact: 'Still' can also mean staying without moving at all.

flyers-stone.definition: a small hard piece of rock

flyers-stone.fact: Ancient people used stone to make their first tools.

flyers-storm.definition: very bad weather with strong wind, rain, or thunder

flyers-storm.fact: A storm can bring loud thunder and bright lightning.

flyers-straight-on.hint: Go straight on until you reach the shop.

flyers-strange.hint: It felt strange to see snow in summer.
flyers-strange.fact: 'Strange' and 'unusual' mean almost the same thing.

flyers-strawberry.hint: Strawberries have tiny seeds on the outside.
flyers-strawberry.fact: Strawberries are the only fruit with seeds on the outside.

flyers-stream.hint: Fish can swim in a small, clear stream.
flyers-stream.fact: Many streams flow into bigger rivers.

flyers-stripe.definition: a long, narrow band of colour
flyers-stripe.hint: A zebra has black and white stripes.
flyers-stripe.fact: Every zebra has its own unique pattern of stripes.

flyers-striped.definition: having long, narrow bands of colour
flyers-striped.hint: A striped T-shirt has lines of different colours.
flyers-striped.fact: Tigers have striped fur to help them hide in tall grass.

flyers-student.definition: a person who is learning at a school or college
flyers-student.hint: Every student in the class has their own desk.
flyers-student.fact: Students learn new things every single day at school.

flyers-study.definition: to spend time learning about a subject
flyers-study.hint: Study a little every day before a big test.
flyers-study.fact: You study best in a quiet place with no distractions.

flyers-subject.definition: an area of knowledge taught at school, like maths
flyers-subject.hint: What is your favourite subject at school?
flyers-subject.fact: Schools usually teach many different subjects every week.

flyers-suddenly.hint: Suddenly, the rain started to pour down.
flyers-suddenly.fact: 'Suddenly' makes a story feel exciting and surprising.

flyers-sugar.definition: a sweet substance added to food and drinks
flyers-sugar.hint: A little sugar makes tea taste sweeter.
flyers-sugar.fact: Sugar is made from plants like sugar cane or sugar beet.

flyers-suitcase.definition: a case used to carry clothes when travelling
flyers-suitcase.hint: Pack your clothes in a suitcase before a holiday.
flyers-suitcase.fact: Suitcases often have wheels so they are easy to pull.

flyers-summer.definition: the warmest season of the year
flyers-summer.hint: Children often swim outside during the summer.
flyers-summer.fact: Summer has the longest days of sunlight in the year.

flyers-sunglasses.definition: dark glasses that protect your eyes from the sun
flyers-sunglasses.hint: Wear sunglasses on a bright, sunny day.
flyers-sunglasses.fact: Sunglasses protect your eyes from strong sunlight.

flyers-sure.hint: Say 'I'm sure' when you have no doubt at all.
flyers-sure.fact: 'Sure' shows you feel confident about something.

flyers-surname.definition: your family name, the last part of your name
flyers-surname.hint: Your surname is usually the same as your parents'.
flyers-surname.fact: In many countries, your surname comes after your first name.

flyers-surprise.hint: A birthday party can be a lovely surprise.
flyers-surprise.fact: A good surprise can make your whole day feel special.

flyers-swan.definition: a large white bird with a long neck that swims
flyers-swan.hint: A swan glides gracefully across the water.
flyers-swan.fact: Swans usually stay with the same partner for their whole life.

flyers-swing.definition: a seat that hangs and moves back and forth
flyers-swing.hint: You sit on a swing and push with your legs to move.
flyers-swing.fact: Playgrounds almost always have a swing to play on.

flyers-taste.definition: the flavour of food, or the sense used to notice it
flyers-taste.fact: Your tongue can taste sweet, sour, salty, and bitter flavours.

flyers-taxi.definition: a car you pay a driver to take you somewhere
flyers-taxi.hint: You can call a taxi to take you to the airport.
flyers-taxi.fact: In many cities, taxis are a special colour, like yellow.

flyers-team.definition: a group of people who play or work together
flyers-team.hint: Everyone on the team wears the same colour shirt.
flyers-team.fact: Football, basketball, and volleyball are all team sports.

flyers-telephone.definition: a machine used to talk to someone far away
flyers-telephone.hint: You use a telephone to call your friends and family.

flyers-tent.definition: a shelter made of cloth, used for camping
flyers-tent.hint: You sleep in a tent when you go camping.
flyers-tent.fact: A tent can be put up and taken down quickly.

flyers-thank.definition: to tell someone you are grateful
flyers-thank.hint: Always thank someone who gives you a gift.
flyers-thank.fact: Saying 'thank you' is a simple way to be polite.

flyers-theatre.definition: a building where plays and shows are performed
flyers-theatre.hint: You watch actors perform live on stage at a theatre.
flyers-theatre.fact: The oldest theatres were built by the ancient Greeks.

flyers-thousand.hint: A thousand is ten times a hundred.
flyers-thousand.fact: It would take about seventeen minutes to count to a thousand.

flyers-tidy.definition: neat, with everything in its proper place
flyers-tidy.hint: Keep your room tidy by putting toys away.

flyers-time.definition: the thing we measure using clocks and calendars
flyers-time.hint: Look at a clock to check the time.
flyers-time.fact: Time is measured in seconds, minutes, hours, days, and years.

flyers-timetable.definition: a chart that shows when things happen
flyers-timetable.hint: Check your timetable to see your next lesson.
flyers-timetable.fact: Buses and trains also have a timetable showing arrival times.

flyers-toe.definition: one of the five parts at the end of your foot
flyers-toe.hint: You have five toes on each foot.
flyers-toe.fact: Your big toe helps you balance when you walk.

flyers-together.definition: with each other, in the same place or time
flyers-together.hint: Friends like to play games together.
flyers-together.fact: Working together often makes a big job easier.

flyers-tomorrow.hint: Say 'see you tomorrow' at the end of the school day.

flyers-tonight.definition: during the evening or night of today
flyers-tonight.hint: We will watch a film tonight after dinner.
flyers-tonight.fact: 'Tonight' means the night part of the day you are in now.

flyers-torch.definition: a small light you carry and hold in your hand
flyers-torch.hint: Use a torch to find your way in the dark.
flyers-torch.fact: In American English, a torch is usually called a 'flashlight'.

flyers-tortoise.definition: a slow-moving animal with a hard, round shell
flyers-tortoise.hint: A tortoise can hide its head inside its shell.
flyers-tortoise.fact: Some tortoises can live for more than one hundred years.

flyers-touch.definition: to put your hand or fingers on something
flyers-touch.hint: Touch the sand gently to feel how soft it is.
flyers-touch.fact: Your fingertips are very good at feeling small details.

flyers-tour.definition: a trip to see the interesting parts of a place
flyers-tour.hint: A guide leads you around on a tour of the museum.
flyers-tour.fact: You can take a tour of a city, a castle, or even a factory.

flyers-traffic.definition: all the cars and other vehicles on a road
flyers-traffic.hint: There is a lot of traffic on the road after school.
flyers-traffic.fact: Traffic lights help control busy traffic safely.

flyers-trainers.definition: soft, comfortable shoes worn for sport
flyers-trainers.hint: Wear trainers for PE so you can run comfortably.
flyers-trainers.fact: 'Trainers' in British English are called 'sneakers' in American English.

flyers-tune.definition: a simple, pleasant series of musical notes
flyers-tune.hint: You can hum a happy tune.
flyers-tune.fact: A catchy tune is one that stays in your head all day!

flyers-turn.definition: to change direction, or move around a point
flyers-turn.hint: Turn left at the corner to reach the park.
flyers-turn.fact: A wheel turns round and round as a bike moves forward.

flyers-turn-off.definition: to stop something working by using a switch
flyers-turn-off.hint: Turn off the light when you leave the room.
flyers-turn-off.fact: 'Turn off' is the opposite of 'turn on'.

flyers-turn-on.definition: to make something start working by using a switch
flyers-turn-on.hint: Turn on the TV to watch your favourite show.
flyers-turn-on.fact: 'Turn on' is the opposite of 'turn off'.

flyers-twice.hint: Brush your teeth twice a day, morning and night.

flyers-tyre.definition: the round rubber part around a wheel
flyers-tyre.hint: A bicycle needs air inside its tyres.
flyers-tyre.fact: Cars usually have four tyres, but bicycles only have two.

flyers-umbrella.definition: something you hold over your head to stay dry in rain
flyers-umbrella.hint: Take an umbrella if it looks like it might rain.
flyers-umbrella.fact: An umbrella can also protect you from strong sunshine.

flyers-unfriendly.definition: not kind or pleasant to other people
flyers-unfriendly.hint: Try not to be unfriendly, even when you feel grumpy.

flyers-unhappy.hint: A kind word can cheer up someone who feels unhappy.

flyers-uniform.definition: special matching clothes worn by a group, like at school
flyers-uniform.hint: You wear a school uniform to look the same as your classmates.
flyers-uniform.fact: Police officers, pilots, and nurses all wear a uniform for work.

flyers-university.definition: a place where people study after college, for a degree
flyers-university.hint: People often go to university when they are about eighteen.
flyers-university.fact: Some universities are hundreds of years old.

flyers-unkind.definition: not nice or caring towards other people
flyers-unkind.hint: It's never nice to be unkind to a friend.

flyers-untidy.definition: messy, not neat or in order
flyers-untidy.hint: Tidy up your untidy room before your friend visits.

flyers-unusual.hint: A purple cat would be a very unusual sight!

flyers-use.definition: to do something with an object for a purpose
flyers-use.hint: You use a pencil to write your name.
flyers-use.fact: You use different tools for different jobs.

flyers-usually.definition: most of the time, as a habit
flyers-usually.hint: I usually go to bed at eight o'clock.
flyers-usually.fact: 'Usually' tells us what happens most of the time, not always.

flyers-view.definition: what you can see from a certain place
flyers-view.hint: You get a great view of the town from the top of the hill.
flyers-view.fact: Tall towers often have the best views of a city.

flyers-violin.definition: a wooden musical instrument played with a bow
flyers-violin.hint: You hold a violin under your chin and play it with a bow.
flyers-violin.fact: A violin has four strings that make different notes.

flyers-visit.definition: to go and see a person or place
flyers-visit.hint: We visit our grandparents on the weekend.
flyers-visit.fact: People visit museums to learn about history and art.

flyers-volleyball.definition: a game where two teams hit a ball over a net
flyers-volleyball.hint: In volleyball, you hit the ball over the net without letting it drop.
flyers-volleyball.fact: Volleyball can be played indoors or on a sandy beach.

flyers-waiter.definition: a person who brings food to tables in a restaurant
flyers-waiter.hint: A waiter takes your order and brings your food.
flyers-waiter.fact: Remember to say 'thank you' to the waiter who serves you.

flyers-warm.definition: having a comfortable, pleasant amount of heat
flyers-warm.hint: Wear a jumper to stay warm in autumn.
flyers-warm.fact: 'Warm' is more comfortable than 'hot' but not 'cold'.

flyers-way.definition: a route or direction to somewhere
flyers-way.hint: Ask 'Which way is the park?' if you are lost.
flyers-way.fact: 'Way' can mean a direction, or a way of doing something.

flyers-west.definition: the direction where the sun sets
flyers-west.hint: The sun sets in the west every evening.
flyers-west.fact: West is the opposite direction to east.

flyers-wheel.definition: a round object that turns to help things move
flyers-wheel.hint: A car has four wheels, and a bicycle has two.
flyers-wheel.fact: The wheel is one of the most important inventions ever made.

flyers-whisper.definition: to speak very quietly and softly
flyers-whisper.hint: Whisper in the library so you don't disturb others.
flyers-whisper.fact: It is hard for other people to hear you when you whisper.

flyers-whistle.definition: to make a high sound by blowing air through your lips
flyers-whistle.hint: A referee will whistle to stop the game.
flyers-whistle.fact: Some birds can whistle beautiful tunes too.

flyers-wife.definition: the woman someone is married to
flyers-wife.hint: A husband and wife are a married couple.
flyers-wife.fact: A wife is part of a person's close family.

flyers-wifi.definition: a way to connect to the internet without wires
flyers-wifi.hint: You need wifi to use the internet on a tablet.
flyers-wifi.fact: 'Wifi' lets many devices connect to the internet at the same time.

flyers-wild.definition: living freely in nature, not kept as a pet
flyers-wild.hint: Lions and tigers are wild animals, not pets.

flyers-will.definition: used to talk about what happens in the future
flyers-will.hint: Say 'I will help you' to promise something in the future.
flyers-will.fact: 'Will' is one of the main ways to talk about the future.

flyers-win.definition: to come first or be the best in a game or contest
flyers-win.hint: You win a race by finishing before everyone else.

flyers-wing.definition: the part of a bird or insect used for flying
flyers-wing.hint: A bird flaps its wings to fly.
flyers-wing.fact: Planes have wings too, just like birds!

flyers-winner.definition: the person or team who wins
flyers-winner.hint: The winner of the race gets a shiny medal.
flyers-winner.fact: Every competition has a winner at the very end.

flyers-winter.definition: the coldest season of the year
flyers-winter.hint: It can snow during winter in some countries.
flyers-winter.fact: Some animals sleep through the whole winter.

flyers-wish.definition: a hope for something you want to happen
flyers-wish.hint: Make a wish before you blow out your birthday candles.
flyers-wish.fact: People often wish on a falling star.

flyers-wonderful.definition: extremely good, causing wonder or joy
flyers-wonderful.hint: Say 'what a wonderful surprise!' when something great happens.

flyers-wood.definition: the hard material that trees are made of
flyers-wood.hint: Chairs and tables are often made of wood.
flyers-wood.fact: Wood comes from trees and can be used to build houses.

flyers-wool.definition: soft, warm material made from sheep's hair
flyers-wool.hint: A woolly jumper keeps you warm in winter.
flyers-wool.fact: Wool comes from the fluffy coat of a sheep.

flyers-worried.definition: feeling anxious about something that might go wrong
flyers-worried.hint: Talk to someone if you feel worried about something.
flyers-worried.fact: Everyone feels worried sometimes — it's a normal feeling.

flyers-x-ray.definition: a picture doctors take to see inside your body
flyers-x-ray.hint: Doctors use an x-ray to check if a bone is broken.
flyers-x-ray.fact: An x-ray can see straight through your skin to your bones.

flyers-yet.definition: up until now, used mostly in questions and negatives
flyers-yet.hint: Say 'not yet' when something has not happened.
flyers-yet.fact: 'Yet' usually goes at the end of a question or sentence.

flyers-yoghurt.definition: a thick, creamy food made from milk
flyers-yoghurt.hint: Yoghurt can be plain or flavoured with fruit.
flyers-yoghurt.fact: Yoghurt is made by adding good bacteria to milk.

flyers-zero.hint: A rocket launch counts down to zero before it blasts off.
flyers-zero.fact: Zero was invented as a number a very long time ago.
